During his tenure as Apple CEO, one of Tim Cook's most delicate tasks was walking a tightrope between defending the company's values and avoiding offending the White House, on issues ranging from immigration policy to diversity and inclusion.

After transitioning to the newly created role of executive chairman, he retains the responsibility of liaising with the government, providing a degree of protection for his successor as CEO, John Ternus……

Past challenges

The challenges Cook has faced date back years. For example, in 2018, changes to U.S. immigration policy and measures affected thousands of Apple employees. Cook at the time joined other CEOs in writing to the government, pointing out that the changes caused "deep concern among many Apple employees" and carried "the risk of disrupting company operations."

Last year, Cook faced a similar dilemma when Trump demanded Apple abandon its diversity and inclusion policies. In response, Cook said the company would comply with any legal changes, but would not abandon its own values.

Cook is now Apple's official diplomat

Apple has confirmed that Cook's new responsibilities include liaising with governments around the world.

Attending a White House dinner next week

Bloomberg reported that Cook will attend the White House state dinner for the Chinese president being held next week. U.S.-China relations are currently at a tense juncture, particularly on the issue of artificial intelligence.

9to5Mac's view

I would venture to speculate that the idea of Cook taking on a diplomatic role was his own proposal. This is a selfless act aimed at shielding his successor from unnecessary distractions and controversy.

Of course, Ternus will still face constraints when responding to controversial policies and laws in the U.S., China, or elsewhere. But handing the responsibility of official responses to someone else does indeed give him more room to manoeuvre.
